findings.title: Python 3.7 is end-of-life
findings.description: Python 3.7.9 (release line 3.7) reached end-of-life on 2023-06-27. It no longer receives security fixes, so known vulnerabilities in it stay unpatched.

impact.technical: Unpatched vulnerabilities and increasing incompatibility with current libraries and platforms.
impact.business: Security and compliance exposure that grows over time, and upgrades that get larger the longer they are postponed.

remediation.summary: Upgrade Python to a supported release line (see https://endoflife.date/python) and test the application against it.

findings.false_positive_guidance: If the declared version is only a minimum (e.g. >=12) and production runs a newer release, update the declaration to match.

findings.title: Flask 1.0 has 4 known vulnerabilities
findings.description:
- GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq (high, CVSS 7.5) CVE-2023-30861, PYSEC-2023-62: Flask vulnerable to possible disclosure of permanent session cookie due to missing Vary: Cookie header
- PYSEC-2026-2151 (medium, CVSS 4.3) CVE-2026-27205, GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726: Flask is a web server gateway interface (WSGI) web application framework
- PYSEC-2023-62 (medium) CVE-2023-30861, GHSA-m2qf-hxjv-5gpq: Flask is a lightweight WSGI web application framework
- GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 (low) CVE-2026-27205, PYSEC-2026-2151: Flask session does not add `Vary: Cookie` header when accessed in some ways

rule.name: Flask vulnerable to possible disclosure of permanent session cookie due to missing Vary: Cookie header

remediation.summary: Upgrade Flask to 3.1.3 or later and re-run the tests.

findings.false_positive_guidance: Advisories match on version only. Check whether the vulnerable function is reachable in this application before deprioritising.

findings.title: Flask 1.0 is end-of-life
findings.description: Flask 1.0 (release line 1.0) is no longer supported by its maintainers. It no longer receives security fixes, so known vulnerabilities in it stay unpatched. Pallets supports only the latest feature release.

impact.technical: Unpatched vulnerabilities and increasing incompatibility with current libraries and platforms.
impact.business: Security and compliance exposure that grows over time, and upgrades that get larger the longer they are postponed.

remediation.summary: Upgrade Flask to a supported release line (see https://flask.palletsprojects.com/en/stable/changes/) and test the application against it.

findings.false_positive_guidance: If the declared version is only a minimum (e.g. >=12) and production runs a newer release, update the declaration to match.

findings.title: No README
findings.description: There is no README explaining what the project is, how to build it and how to run it.

remediation.summary: Add a README with purpose, setup, build, test and deployment instructions.
